summary.title: Speculative Execution Side Channel Mitigations
summary.one_liner: Intel's technical guidance explaining branch target injection, bounds check bypass, and speculative store bypass, and the IBRS, STIBP, IBPB and LFENCE-based mitigations for them.
keywords: how to mitigate spectre in software
predictor mode host guest user supervisor
takeaways: Branch target injection exploits shared indirect branch predictors; IBRS, STIBP and IBPB are the three indirect branch control mechanisms Intel defines against it.
IBRS restricts indirect branch speculation, STIBP limits predictor sharing between sibling hyperthreads on a core, and IBPB is a command that creates a barrier between software contexts.
STIBP carries a significant performance cost on existing Core-family processors, so the document advises against setting it during all application execution.
Enhanced IBRS can be set once and left on, avoiding repeated WRMSR costs on ring transitions, and makes STIBP unnecessary when IBRS is set.
Bounds check bypass is mitigated in software by inserting an LFENCE or other serializing instruction between a bounds check and the dependent load.
summary.summary: This Intel revision 2.0 document (originally published May 2018) describes three transient execution side channels: branch target injection, bounds check bypass, and speculative store bypass. It explains the indirect branch control mechanisms (IBRS, STIBP, IBPB), how they depend on privilege-based predictor modes and Hyper-Threading sharing, and how retpoline offers a software alternative. For bounds check bypass it recommends LFENCE or serializing instructions and gives a CMOV-based example, with further sections on speculative store bypass and CPUID/MSR enumeration. The page is a dense specification-style reference rather than a step-by-step tutorial.
